title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Wisdom Of The Afternoon Prayer

questions.question: What time of day is this passage about?
questions.answer: It is about the afternoon prayer time.

questions.question: What season does this time make a person think about?
questions.answer: It makes a person think about fall.

questions.question: What part of life does this time also remind a person of?
questions.answer: It reminds a person of old age.

questions.question: What does the lowering sun teach about people and worldly things?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are like guests and that worldly things do not last.

questions.question: Why do these blessings feel important by that time of day?
questions.answer: Because many of them have gathered through the whole day.

questions.question: What does the human soul want, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It wants what lasts forever.

questions.question: How does the soul feel about parting?
questions.answer: It feels hurt by it.

questions.question: Why is the afternoon prayer called a fitting duty for a person?
questions.answer: Because it is a good way to thank Allah and do what a human being should do.

questions.question: When a person makes du'a then, whose mercy does he seek shelter in?
questions.answer: Allah’s endless mercy.

questions.question: What should a person do because of the many blessings received?
questions.answer: Praise Allah and thank Him.

questions.question: What does bowing show?
questions.answer: It shows humility before Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: What does prostration show in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows deep humility before Allah’s everlasting divinity.

questions.question: What does a person find through this prayer?
questions.answer: Comfort in the heart and peace in the soul.

questions.question: How does this prayer prepare a person after giving comfort?
questions.answer: It gets the person ready to worship Allah.

questions.question: Which prayer is being explained in the passage?
questions.answer: The Asr prayer.

questions.question: What is happening to the day when this prayer time comes?
questions.answer: The day’s matters are coming to an end.

questions.question: What does the sun beginning to go down hint about life in this world?
questions.answer: Life here is temporary.

questions.question: How are human beings described in this world?
questions.answer: They are described as guests with duties.

questions.question: What does the passage say the soul was made for?
questions.answer: It was made for everlasting life.

questions.question: What kind treatment does the soul love?
questions.answer: It loves kindness.

questions.question: What hurts the soul?
questions.answer: Being separated.

questions.question: Why can this prayer be a joyful act even though the time feels sad?
questions.answer: Because it brings a person near Allah and gives inner peace.

questions.question: Where does a person turn in prayer at this time?
questions.answer: To Allah’s eternal court.

questions.question: What is one thing a person does with words in this prayer?
questions.answer: The person asks Allah and praises Him.

questions.question: What is one thing a person does with the body in this prayer?
questions.answer: The person bows and prostrates.

questions.question: Why does a person bow humbly?
questions.answer: To show lowliness before Allah’s great power and rule.

questions.question: What comes to the heart through this worship?
questions.answer: True comfort.

questions.question: What comes to the spirit through this worship?
questions.answer: Ease and calm.

questions.question: What main idea does the passage teach about the afternoon prayer?
questions.answer: It teaches that the afternoon prayer is very suitable and helpful at that time of day.

questions.question: What feelings can the afternoon time bring to mind?
questions.answer: It can bring serious and sad thoughts.

questions.question: Why might this time remind someone of fall?
questions.answer: Because it points to things fading and moving toward an end.

questions.question: What part of the day is finishing by then?
questions.answer: The work and events of the day.

questions.question: What has built up by that time from the whole day?
questions.answer: Many blessings from Allah.

questions.question: Name one blessing listed in the passage.
questions.answer: Good health.

questions.question: What does the sinking sun suggest about all created things?
questions.answer: They change and do not stay forever.

questions.question: What does the soul seek that this world cannot fully give?
questions.answer: Something everlasting.

questions.question: If a person knows blessings have piled up, what should that person do?
questions.answer: Thank and praise Allah.

questions.question: If a person feels weak before Allah’s greatness, what action in prayer fits that feeling?
questions.answer: Bowing.

questions.question: If a person feels very humble before Allah, what other action in prayer fits that feeling?
questions.answer: Prostration.

questions.question: What kind of mercy does the worshipper hope for?
questions.answer: Mercy with no end.

questions.question: What two good results does the passage mention after this prayer?
questions.answer: Peace inside and readiness to worship.

questions.question: Is this prayer shown as only a burden, or also as a delight?
questions.answer: It is shown as a delight too.

questions.question: Why is it wise to pray at this time instead of ignoring it?
questions.answer: Because it helps a person remember Allah, thank Him, and find comfort.

questions.question: What does the passage say the afternoon time makes people remember about life?
questions.answer: It makes them remember that life moves toward its later stages and ending.

questions.question: What picture in the sky helps teach that lesson?
questions.answer: The sun going down.

questions.question: What does that picture teach about this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that this world does not remain the same forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say has become a large amount by afternoon?
questions.answer: The blessings given during the day.

questions.question: Give one example of those blessings.
questions.answer: Well-being.

questions.question: How should a person respond to many blessings from Allah?
questions.answer: By thanking and praising Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the human spirit and foreverness?
questions.answer: It says the spirit longs for forever.

questions.question: What kind of things make the spirit sad?
questions.answer: Times of separation.

questions.question: What does it mean to take refuge in Allah’s mercy at this time?
questions.answer: It means turning to Allah for care and help.

questions.question: In the passage, why is bowing important during this prayer?
questions.answer: Because it shows humble respect before Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: In the passage, why is prostration important during this prayer?
questions.answer: Because it shows complete humility before Allah.

questions.question: What happens inside the person after praying this way?
questions.answer: The person feels comforted and calm.

questions.question: What does “being ready for worship” mean here?
questions.answer: It means becoming prepared to serve Allah with respect.

questions.question: Would this prayer fit a person who wants to remember Allah at the end of the day’s work?
questions.answer: Yes, because it comes as the day’s matters are wrapping up.

questions.question: What is one reason this prayer is called fitting for a true human being?
questions.answer: Because it matches the human need to thank Allah and seek lasting peace.

questions.question: What prayer time is described as coming in the afternoon?
questions.answer: Asr time.

questions.question: What three things does this time call to mind?
questions.answer: Fall, old age, and the late ending of the world.

questions.question: What is happening to the day itself at this hour?
questions.answer: It is nearing its close.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention blessings at this time?
questions.answer: Because the day’s blessings can now be seen as many together.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the sun starting to set?
questions.answer: Human life is temporary and worldly things pass away.

questions.question: What does the human spirit deeply want?
questions.answer: Everlasting life.

questions.question: What kind of action is the afternoon prayer said to be for a human being?
questions.answer: A noble and proper act of worship.

questions.question: What does this prayer help a person repay?
questions.answer: A duty that comes with being human.

questions.question: To whom does a person turn when making du'a at this time?
questions.answer: To Allah, the Everlasting One.

questions.question: What should come with thanks for blessings in this prayer?
questions.answer: Praise.

questions.question: What feeling should a person have while bowing?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What feeling should a person have while prostrating?
questions.answer: Very deep humility.

questions.question: What does the person gain in the heart from this prayer?
questions.answer: Real comfort.

questions.question: Is the passage about morning, noon, or afternoon prayer?
questions.answer: It is about afternoon prayer.

questions.question: What season is used as an example of sadness and fading?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: What age period in a person’s life is mentioned with this time?
questions.answer: Old age.

questions.question: What bigger ending is also mentioned besides the ending of a day?
questions.answer: The ending time of the world.

questions.question: By afternoon, what has happened to the day’s tasks?
questions.answer: They have mostly reached their finish.

questions.question: By afternoon, what has happened to the day’s blessings?
questions.answer: They have added up into a great amount.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a human being in this world?
questions.answer: Like a guest with responsibilities.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the things of this world?
questions.answer: They are passing and always changing.

questions.question: Why does the soul need something more than temporary things?
questions.answer: Because it was made to want what lasts forever.

questions.question: What makes the soul ache according to the passage?
questions.answer: Separation.

questions.question: What makes the afternoon prayer suitable for this time?
questions.answer: It helps a person turn to Allah when thinking about endings and blessings.

questions.question: What does a person seek by making du'a then?
questions.answer: Shelter in Allah’s endless mercy.

questions.question: What does a person do because Allah has given so many blessings?
questions.answer: The person gives thanks and praise.

questions.question: What do bowing and prostrating together show?
questions.answer: They show humility before Allah’s greatness and everlastingness.

questions.question: What final good change does this prayer bring to the worshipper?
questions.answer: It brings comfort and prepares the person for worship.
